sentences.t: Da gab er sich zu erkennen, und seine Eltern fielen ihm vor Freude um den Hals,
sentences.l: Then he made himself known, and his parents fell about his neck for joy,
sentences.i: Then he made himself known, and his parents fell on his neck for joy,
sentences.n: “sich zu erkennen geben” is the fixed phrase for revealing who one is. “fielen ihm … um den Hals” is the dative of possession: fell about the neck to him, that is, embraced him. “vor Freude” = for joy, out of joy.

sentences.t: und er war so bewegt in seinem Herzen, daß er sie auf beide Wangen küßte und an die Worte des Mädchens nicht dachte.
sentences.l: and he was so moved in his heart that he kissed them on both cheeks and did not think of the girl’s words.
sentences.i: and he was so moved in his heart that he kissed them on both cheeks and never thought of the girl’s words.
sentences.n: Both cheeks includes the right one. The tale lets the warning break itself in a single clause, without a word of comment, and the reader is left to feel the drop.

sentences.t: Wie er ihnen aber den Kuß auf die rechte Wange gegeben hatte, verschwand ihm jeder Gedanke an die Königstochter.
sentences.l: But as he had given them the kiss on the right cheek, every thought of the king’s daughter vanished from him.
sentences.i: But once he had given them the kiss on the right cheek, every thought of the king’s daughter vanished from him.
sentences.n: “wie” once more means as, the moment that. “verschwand ihm” is the dative of the person affected: vanished from him. “Kuß” is the 1857 spelling of Kuss.

sentences.t: Er leerte seine Taschen aus und legte Händevoll der größten Edelsteine auf den Tisch.
sentences.l: He emptied out his pockets and laid handfuls of the largest precious stones on the table.
sentences.i: He emptied out his pockets and laid handfuls of the largest jewels on the table.
sentences.n: ausleeren is separable: leerte … aus. “Händevoll” is written as one word here — the plural of eine Handvoll, a handful.

sentences.t: Die Eltern wußten gar nicht was sie mit dem Reichthum anfangen sollten.
sentences.l: The parents did not know at all what they should do with the wealth.
sentences.i: The parents had no notion what to do with such wealth.
sentences.n: “gar nicht” = not at all. “mit etwas anfangen” is the idiom for knowing what to do with something. “Reichthum” is the 1857 spelling of Reichtum.

sentences.t: Da baute der Vater ein prächtiges Schloß, von Gärten, Wäldern und Wiesen umgeben, als wenn ein Fürst darin wohnen sollte.
sentences.l: Then the father built a splendid castle, surrounded by gardens, woods and meadows, as if a prince were to live in it.
sentences.i: Then the father built a splendid castle surrounded by gardens, woods and meadows, as though a prince were to live in it.
sentences.n: Here “Schloß” is the castle sense of the word — the 1857 spelling of Schloss. “als wenn … sollte” is the subjunctive of comparison: as if it were meant for a prince.

sentences.t: Und als es fertig war, sagte die Mutter „ich habe ein Mädchen für dich ausgesucht, in drei Tagen soll die Hochzeit sein.“
sentences.l: And when it was ready, the mother said “I have picked out a girl for you, in three days the wedding shall be.”
sentences.i: And when it was finished, the mother said “I have chosen a girl for you; in three days the wedding is to be.”
sentences.n: aussuchen is separable: to pick out, select. The marriage is arranged for him and the tale reports it without a flicker of objection from anyone.

sentences.t: Der Sohn war mit allem zufrieden, was die Eltern wollten.
sentences.l: The son was content with everything that the parents wanted.
sentences.i: The son was content with whatever his parents wished.
sentences.n: With his memory gone he has no will of his own in the matter, and the sentence says so without saying so.

sentences.t: Die arme Königstochter hatte lange vor der Stadt gestanden und auf die Rückkehr des Jünglings gewartet.
sentences.l: The poor king’s daughter had stood long before the town and waited for the return of the youth.
sentences.i: The poor king’s daughter had stood a long while outside the town, waiting for the young man’s return.
sentences.n: “auf … warten” is the standard frame: to wait for. der Jüngling is a young man, more elevated than junger Mann.

sentences.t: Als es Abend ward, sprach sie „gewis hat er seine Eltern auf die rechte Wange geküßt, und hat mich vergessen.“
sentences.l: When it became evening, she said “surely he has kissed his parents on the right cheek, and has forgotten me.”
sentences.i: When evening came she said “he must have kissed his parents on the right cheek, and forgotten me.”
sentences.n: “ward” is the archaic past of werden. “gewis” is the 1857 spelling of gewiß, here meaning surely, no doubt — a guess spoken as near certainty.

sentences.t: Ihr Herz war voll Trauer,
sentences.l: Her heart was full of sorrow,
sentences.n: “voll Trauer” takes the bare noun with no article and no case ending — full of sorrow, an old construction German still allows after voll.

sentences.t: sie wünschte sich in ein einsames Waldhäuschen und wollte nicht wieder an den Hof ihres Vaters zurück.
sentences.l: she wished herself into a lonely little forest house and would not go back again to her father’s court.
sentences.i: she wished herself into a lonely little house in the forest, and would not return to her father’s court.
sentences.n: “wollte nicht … zurück” has no verb of motion: wollen and the little word zurück carry it between them. Her ring can grant any wish, and what she asks for is a hut.

sentences.t: Jeden Abend gieng sie in die Stadt, und gieng an seinem Haus vorüber:
sentences.l: Every evening she went into the town, and went past his house:
sentences.i: Every evening she went into the town and past his house:
sentences.n: vorübergehen is separable: gieng … vorüber. “jeden Abend” is a bare accusative of time — every evening.

sentences.t: er sah sie manchmal, aber er kannte sie nicht mehr.
sentences.l: he saw her sometimes, but he knew her no more.
sentences.i: he saw her sometimes, but he no longer knew her.
sentences.n: kennen is to know a person by acquaintance, as against wissen, to know a fact — the distinction English does not mark.

sentences.t: Endlich hörte sie wie die Leute sagten „morgen wird seine Hochzeit gefeiert.“
sentences.l: At last she heard how the people said “tomorrow his wedding will be celebrated.”
sentences.i: At last she heard the people saying “tomorrow his wedding is to be celebrated.”
sentences.n: “hörte … wie” again — heard how they said it, where English uses a bare participle. “wird … gefeiert” is the passive with werden.

sentences.t: Da sprach sie „ich will versuchen ob ich sein Herz wieder gewinne.“
sentences.l: Then she said “I will try whether I win his heart again.”
sentences.i: Then she said “I will try whether I can win his heart back.”
sentences.n: “ob” = whether. gewinnen is to win, to gain; the present tense stands where English wants a modal, “whether I can win”.

sentences.t: Als der erste Hochzeitstag gefeiert ward, da drehte sie ihren Wunschring und sprach „ein Kleid so glänzend wie die Sonne.“
sentences.l: When the first wedding day was celebrated, she turned her wishing-ring and said “a dress as gleaming as the sun.”
sentences.i: When the first day of the wedding was being celebrated, she turned her wishing-ring and said “a dress as gleaming as the sun.”
sentences.n: A wedding of several days is the older custom the tale assumes without explaining. The wish is a bare noun phrase — no verb, no please, just the thing named.

sentences.t: Alsbald lag das Kleid vor ihr und war so glänzend, als wenn es aus lauter Sonnenstrahlen gewebt wäre.
sentences.l: At once the dress lay before her and was so gleaming as if it were woven out of nothing but sunbeams.
sentences.i: At once the dress lay before her, as gleaming as though it were woven of nothing but sunbeams.
sentences.n: “lauter” before a noun means nothing but, sheer. “gewebt wäre” is the subjunctive of comparison after als wenn.

sentences.t: Als alle Gäste sich versammelt hatten, so trat sie in den Saal.
sentences.l: When all the guests had assembled themselves, she stepped into the hall.
sentences.i: When all the guests had gathered, she stepped into the hall.
sentences.n: sich versammeln is reflexive where English uses the plain intransitive: to assemble. The “so” opening the main clause merely answers the when-clause.

sentences.t: Jedermann wunderte sich über das schöne Kleid, am meisten die Braut,
sentences.l: Everyone wondered at the beautiful dress, most of all the bride,
sentences.i: Everyone marvelled at the beautiful dress, the bride most of all,
sentences.n: sich wundern über is to be astonished at. “am meisten” is the superlative of viel used adverbially: most of all.

sentences.t: und da schöne Kleider ihre größte Lust waren, so gieng sie zu der Fremden und fragte ob sie es ihr verkaufen wollte.
sentences.l: and since beautiful dresses were her greatest delight, she went to the stranger and asked whether she would sell it to her.
sentences.i: and since fine dresses were her greatest delight, she went to the stranger and asked whether she would sell it to her.
sentences.n: “da” at the head of a clause is since, because. “die Fremde” is an adjective used as a noun — the strange woman, the stranger.

sentences.t: „Für Geld nicht,“ antwortete sie, „aber wenn ich die erste Nacht vor der Thüre verweilen darf, wo der Bräutigam schläft, so will ich es hingeben.“
sentences.l: “Not for money,” answered she, “but if I may stay the first night before the door where the bridegroom sleeps, then I will give it up.”
sentences.i: “Not for money,” she answered, “but if I may spend the first night at the door where the bridegroom sleeps, I will hand it over.”
sentences.n: weilen returns here from the first block, again for staying or lingering. hingeben is separable: to give away, hand over. The bargain is repeated with only small changes for each of the three nights.

sentences.t: Die Braut konnte ihr Verlangen nicht bezwingen und willigte ein,
sentences.l: The bride could not master her craving and consented,
sentences.i: The bride could not master her craving and agreed,
sentences.n: einwilligen is separable: willigte … ein. das Verlangen is the noun from verlangen — a longing, a craving.

sentences.t: aber sie mischte dem Bräutigam einen Schlaftrunk in seinen Nachtwein, wovon er in tiefen Schlaf verfiel.
sentences.l: but she mixed the bridegroom a sleeping-draught into his night wine, whereof he fell into a deep sleep.
sentences.i: but she mixed a sleeping-draught into the bridegroom’s night wine, from which he fell into a deep sleep.
sentences.n: “wovon” = whereof, from which — wo(r)- plus a preposition, the relative counterpart of da(r)-. der Nachtwein is the wine drunk last thing before bed. “dem Bräutigam” is a dative of the person concerned: mixed it for him, into his.

sentences.t: Als nun alles still geworden war, so kauerte sich die Königstochter vor die Thüre der Schlafkammer, öffnete sie ein wenig und rief hinein
sentences.l: When now everything had become still, the king’s daughter crouched down before the door of the bedchamber, opened it a little and called in
sentences.i: When at last everything had gone quiet, the king’s daughter crouched down before the door of the bedchamber, opened it a little and called in
sentences.n: sich kauern is to crouch, to squat down. “rief hinein” ends the block on the separable particle and runs straight into the song that follows — the printing gives it no full stop at all.

sentences.t:
„Trommler, Trommler, hör mich an,
hast du mich denn ganz vergessen?
sentences.l:
“Drummer, drummer, hear me out,
have you then quite forgotten me?
sentences.i:
“Drummer, drummer, give me a hearing,
have you forgotten me altogether?
sentences.n: A sung call breaks into the prose here, and the lineation is the 1857 printing’s own. The German rhymes — vergessen with gesessen, Leben with gegeben in the lines that follow — while “hör mich an” frames the whole; Lectorium’s idiomatic layer does not rhyme, so the English gives the sense plainly and lets the note carry the music. anhören is separable: hör … an, hear me out. “denn” is a flavouring particle with no English word of its own; it colours the question with reproach.

sentences.t:
hast du auf dem Glasberg nicht bei mir gesessen?
habe ich vor der Hexe nicht bewahrt dein Leben?
hast du mir auf Treue nicht die Hand gegeben?
Trommler, Trommler, hör mich an.“
sentences.l:
did you not sit beside me on the glass mountain?
did I not guard your life from the witch?
did you not give me your hand upon faith?
Drummer, drummer, hear me out.”
sentences.i:
did you not sit at my side on the glass mountain?
did I not keep your life safe from the witch?
did you not give me your hand and pledge your faith?
Drummer, drummer, give me a hearing.”
sentences.n: This is the same call going on, and the printing sets it as a separate verse block without repeating the opening two lines. “auf Treue die Hand geben” is the same gesture as “versprach ihr in die Hand” earlier — to give one’s hand as a pledge of faith. bewahren vor = to keep safe from. In the fourth line the past participle “bewahrt” stands before its object, which German verse allows for the sake of the rhyme and German prose would not.

sentences.t: Aber es war alles vergeblich, der Trommler wachte nicht auf,
sentences.l: But it was all in vain, the drummer did not wake up,
sentences.n: aufwachen is separable: wachte … auf. “vergeblich” returns from the drummer’s own attempt to climb the mountain — the tale reuses its words deliberately.

sentences.t: und als der Morgen anbrach, mußte die Königstochter unverrichteter Dinge wieder fortgehen.
sentences.l: and when the morning broke, the king’s daughter had to go away again with nothing accomplished.
sentences.i: and when morning broke, the king’s daughter had to go away again with nothing gained.
sentences.n: anbrechen is separable: brach … an, of day breaking. “unverrichteter Dinge” is a fixed genitive phrase — with things unaccomplished, having achieved nothing.

sentences.t: Am zweiten Abend drehte sie ihren Wunschring und sprach „ein Kleid so silbern als der Mond.“
sentences.l: On the second evening she turned her wishing-ring and said “a dress as silver as the moon.”
sentences.i: On the second evening she turned her wishing-ring and said “a dress as silvery as the moon.”
sentences.n: “so silbern als” uses als where modern German would use wie for a comparison of equals; 1857 German allows both. “silbern” is the adjective from Silber.

sentences.t: Als sie mit dem Kleid, das so zart war, wie der Mondschein, bei dem Fest erschien, erregte sie wieder das Verlangen der Braut
sentences.l: When she appeared at the feast with the dress, which was as delicate as the moonlight, she stirred up the bride’s craving again
sentences.i: When she appeared at the feast in the dress, which was as delicate as moonlight, she stirred up the bride’s craving once more
sentences.n: erregen is to arouse, stir up. “das Verlangen der Braut” is a plain genitive: the bride’s craving — the same word used of her the night before.

sentences.t: und gab es ihr für die Erlaubnis auch die zweite Nacht vor der Thüre der Schlafkammer zubringen zu dürfen.
sentences.l: and gave it to her for permission to spend the second night too before the door of the bedchamber.
sentences.i: and gave it to her for leave to spend the second night as well before the door of the bedchamber.
sentences.n: “zubringen zu dürfen” stacks two infinitives: to be allowed to spend. zubringen is separable and means to pass or spend time.

sentences.t: Da rief sie in nächtlicher Stille
sentences.l: Then she called in the stillness of the night
sentences.i: Then in the stillness of the night she called
sentences.n: “in nächtlicher Stille” — die Stille is the noun, stillness, not the adjective still. The sentence has no full stop, because the song follows straight on.

sentences.t:
„Trommler, Trommler, hör mich an,
hast du mich denn ganz vergessen?
hast du auf dem Glasberg nicht bei mir gesessen?
habe ich vor der Hexe nicht bewahrt dein Leben?
hast du mir auf Treue nicht die Hand gegeben?
Trommler, Trommler, hör mich an.“
sentences.l:
“Drummer, drummer, hear me out,
have you then quite forgotten me?
did you not sit beside me on the glass mountain?
did I not guard your life from the witch?
did you not give me your hand upon faith?
Drummer, drummer, hear me out.”
sentences.i:
“Drummer, drummer, give me a hearing,
have you forgotten me altogether?
did you not sit at my side on the glass mountain?
did I not keep your life safe from the witch?
did you not give me your hand and pledge your faith?
Drummer, drummer, give me a hearing.”
sentences.n: The same call as on the first night, now printed whole: the two opening lines and the four that followed them, word for word as before. Because the German has not changed, the English here does not change either — where a line comes back, it comes back in the same words.

sentences.t: Aber der Trommler, von dem Schlaftrunk betäubt, war nicht zu erwecken.
sentences.l: But the drummer, stupefied by the sleeping-draught, was not to be woken.
sentences.i: But the drummer, stupefied by the sleeping-draught, could not be woken.
sentences.n: “war nicht zu erwecken” — was not to be woken — is German’s neat way of saying could not be; sein plus zu plus an infinitive carries a passive possibility.

sentences.t: Traurig gieng sie den Morgen wieder zurück in ihr Waldhaus.
sentences.l: Sadly she went back again in the morning into her forest house.
sentences.i: Sadly she went back to her house in the forest in the morning.
sentences.n: “den Morgen” is a bare accusative of time — in the morning, during the morning.

sentences.t: Aber die Leute im Haus hatten die Klage des fremden Mädchens gehört und erzählten dem Bräutigam davon:
sentences.l: But the people in the house had heard the strange girl’s lament and told the bridegroom of it:
sentences.i: But the people of the house had heard the strange girl’s lament and told the bridegroom about it:
sentences.n: “des fremden Mädchens” is a genitive. “davon” = of it, about it — da(r)- plus a preposition again.

sentences.t: sie sagten ihm auch daß es ihm nicht möglich gewesen wäre etwas davon zu vernehmen, weil sie ihm einen Schlaftrunk in den Wein geschüttet hätten.
sentences.l: they also said to him that it would not have been possible for him to hear anything of it, because they had poured a sleeping-draught into his wine.
sentences.i: they told him too that he could not possibly have heard any of it, because a sleeping-draught had been poured into his wine.
sentences.n: “gewesen wäre” and “geschüttet hätten” are both subjunctive, and that is the whole signal that this is reported speech: German marks it on the verb rather than with a phrase like “they claimed”. “sie” here is vague — the people of the house, not the bride by name — and the tale leaves it so.

sentences.t: Am dritten Abend drehte die Königstochter den Wunschring und sprach „ein Kleid flimmernd wie Sterne.“
sentences.l: On the third evening the king’s daughter turned the wishing-ring and said “a dress glittering like stars.”
sentences.i: On the third evening the king’s daughter turned the wishing-ring and said “a dress glittering like the stars.”
sentences.n: flimmern is to glimmer or twinkle. The three dresses — sun, moon, stars — are a set that runs through many of these tales; here each buys one night.

sentences.t: Als sie sich darin auf dem Fest zeigte, war die Braut über die Pracht des Kleides, das die andern weit übertraf, ganz außer sich und sprach „ich soll und muß es haben.“
sentences.l: When she showed herself in it at the feast, the bride was quite beside herself over the splendour of the dress, which far surpassed the others, and said “I shall and must have it.”
sentences.i: When she showed herself in it at the feast, the bride was quite beside herself at the splendour of the dress, which far surpassed the others, and said “I shall and must have it.”
sentences.n: “außer sich” = beside oneself. “ich soll und muß” piles two modals with no main verb between them, which German allows and English can copy here word for word.

sentences.t: Das Mädchen gab es, wie die andern, für die Erlaubnis die Nacht vor der Thüre des Bräutigams zuzubringen.
sentences.l: The girl gave it, like the others, for permission to spend the night before the bridegroom’s door.
sentences.i: The girl gave it up, as she had the others, for leave to spend the night before the bridegroom’s door.
sentences.n: “wie die andern” = like the other ones, meaning the other dresses. The bargain is reported in one line the third time, where the first time took several — the tale compresses as it repeats.

sentences.t: Der Bräutigam aber trank den Wein nicht, der ihm vor dem Schlafengehen gereicht wurde, sondern goß ihn hinter das Bett.
sentences.l: But the bridegroom did not drink the wine that was handed to him before going to bed, but poured it behind the bed.
sentences.i: The bridegroom, however, did not drink the wine handed him before he went to bed, but poured it away behind the bed.
sentences.n: “sondern” is the but that follows a negative — not this, but that — and is a different word from “aber”. das Schlafengehen is the infinitive schlafen gehen made into a noun: going to bed. “goß” is the past of gießen.

sentences.t: Und als alles im Haus still geworden war, so hörte er eine sanfte Stimme, die ihn anrief
sentences.l: And when everything in the house had become still, he heard a soft voice that called to him
sentences.i: And when everything in the house had gone quiet, he heard a soft voice calling to him
sentences.n: anrufen is separable: rief … an. “so” opens the main clause and merely answers the when-clause. For the third time the sentence ends without a full stop and runs on into the song.

sentences.t:
„Trommler, Trommler, hör mich an,
hast du mich denn ganz vergessen?
hast du auf dem Glasberg nicht bei mir gesessen?
habe ich vor der Hexe nicht bewahrt dein Leben?
hast du mir auf Treue nicht die Hand gegeben?
Trommler, Trommler, hör mich an.“
sentences.l:
“Drummer, drummer, hear me out,
have you then quite forgotten me?
did you not sit beside me on the glass mountain?
did I not guard your life from the witch?
did you not give me your hand upon faith?
Drummer, drummer, hear me out.”
sentences.i:
“Drummer, drummer, give me a hearing,
have you forgotten me altogether?
did you not sit at my side on the glass mountain?
did I not keep your life safe from the witch?
did you not give me your hand and pledge your faith?
Drummer, drummer, give me a hearing.”
sentences.n: The third and last time, identical again in every word. What has changed is only who is listening: the bridegroom poured his wine away behind the bed.

sentences.t: Plötzlich kam ihm das Gedächtnis wieder.
sentences.l: Suddenly his memory came back to him.
sentences.i: All at once his memory came back.
sentences.n: “kam ihm … wieder” is the dative of the person: came back to him. das Gedächtnis is memory as the faculty of remembering, not a particular recollection.

sentences.t: „Ach,“ rief er, „wie habe ich so treulos handeln können,
sentences.l: “Ah,” he cried, “how could I have acted so faithlessly,
sentences.i: “Ah,” he cried, “how could I have acted so faithlessly!
sentences.n: handeln here means to act, to behave — not the other common sense of the verb, to trade or deal. treulos is the negative of treu, and answers “deine Treue” from the mountain.

sentences.t: aber der Kuß, den ich meinen Eltern in der Freude meines Herzens auf die rechte Wange gegeben habe, der ist Schuld daran, der hat mich betäubt.“
sentences.l: but the kiss that I gave my parents on the right cheek in the joy of my heart, that is to blame for it, that has stupefied me.”
sentences.i: but the kiss I gave my parents on the right cheek in the joy of my heart — that is what is to blame, that is what stunned me.”
sentences.n: “der Kuß …, der ist Schuld daran, der hat mich betäubt” names the subject and then picks it up twice more with “der” — the resumptive pronoun this tale uses constantly. “Schuld an etwas sein” = to be to blame for something. betäuben returns from the sleeping-draught two blocks earlier, now used of the kiss.

sentences.t: Er sprang auf, nahm die Königstochter bei der Hand und führte sie zu dem Bett seiner Eltern.
sentences.l: He sprang up, took the king’s daughter by the hand and led her to the bed of his parents.
sentences.i: He sprang up, took the king’s daughter by the hand and led her to his parents’ bedside.
sentences.n: aufspringen is separable: sprang … auf. “bei der Hand” takes the definite article where English wants a possessive — by the hand, meaning by her hand.

sentences.t: „Das ist meine rechte Braut,“ sprach er, „wenn ich die andere heirathe, so thue ich großes Unrecht.“
sentences.l: “That is my right bride,” said he, “if I marry the other, then I do great wrong.”
sentences.i: “This is my true bride,” said he; “if I marry the other, I do a great wrong.”
sentences.n: “recht” here means right in the sense of rightful, true — the same word that has been marking the fatal right cheek all through the tale. “heirathe” is the 1857 spelling of heirate.

sentences.t: Die Eltern, als sie hörten wie alles sich zugetragen hatte, willigten ein.
sentences.l: The parents, when they heard how everything had come to pass, consented.
sentences.i: The parents, when they heard how it had all come about, gave their consent.
sentences.n: sich zutragen is to come to pass, to happen. einwilligen is separable: willigten … ein, the same verb the bride used when she agreed to the bargain.

sentences.t: Da wurden die Lichter im Saal wieder angezündet, Pauken und Trompeten herbei geholt,
sentences.l: Then the lights in the hall were lit again, kettledrums and trumpets fetched in,
sentences.i: Then the lights in the hall were lit again, kettledrums and trumpets brought in,
sentences.n: A string of passives sharing one “wurden” — lit, fetched, invited, all governed by the same auxiliary far back at the start. “herbei geholt” is two words in 1857 for herbeigeholt.

sentences.t: die Freunde und Verwandten eingeladen wieder zu kommen, und die wahre Hochzeit ward mit großer Freude gefeiert.
sentences.l: the friends and relatives invited to come again, and the true wedding was celebrated with great joy.
sentences.i: the friends and kinsfolk invited back, and the true wedding was celebrated with great joy.
sentences.n: “die wahre Hochzeit” answers “meine rechte Braut” a few lines above. “ward” is the archaic past of werden, here forming the passive.

sentences.t: Die erste Braut behielt die schönen Kleider zur Entschädigung und gab sich zufrieden.
sentences.l: The first bride kept the beautiful dresses as compensation and was content.
sentences.i: The first bride kept the beautiful dresses by way of compensation, and was satisfied.
sentences.n: “zur Entschädigung” = by way of compensation. “gab sich zufrieden” is the fixed phrase for being content with what one gets. The tale ends by settling accounts with the jilted bride in a single clause, and asks no further questions about her.

glossary.arbeiten: die Arbeit — pieces of work, tasks (acc. pl.: drei Arbeiten; not the infinitive arbeiten)
glossary.bleibe: bleiben — (I) stay, remain (1st sg. present; here zurückbleiben: bleibe … zurück, stay behind)
glossary.boshaften: boshaft — spiteful, malicious (adj., dat. pl. here: mit boshaften Augen)
glossary.daran: daran — at it, on it, of it, to it (da(r)- plus an, standing for a thing rather than a person)
glossary.deiner: deiner — your (dein inflected, dat. fem. sg.: aus deiner Noth, bei deiner Ankunft)
glossary.dinge: das Ding — thing (gen. pl. in the fixed phrase unverrichteter Dinge: with nothing accomplished)
glossary.eins: eins — one (neuter pronoun; here one of the Stückchen, the pieces of linen)
glossary.essen: das Essen — food, a meal (the infinitive essen, to eat, used as a noun)
glossary.euch: euch — you, yourselves (acc./dat. plural of ihr; the drummer is addressing more than one giant)
glossary.feines: fein — fine (adj., neut. nom./acc. sg. strong: feines Leinen, fine linen)
glossary.fischen: der Fisch — fish (dat. pl.: einer von den Fischen)
glossary.frage: die Frage — question (noun; die Frage thun, to put the question)
glossary.fund: der Fund — find, the thing found (masc. noun, from finden)
glossary.gefallen: das Gefallen — favour, kindness (noun; jemandem etwas zu Gefallen thun, to do someone a favour)
glossary.geht: gehen — goes, runs (3rd sg. present; of a road: der Weg geht durch, the road goes through)
glossary.gesellen: der Geselle — fellow, companion (acc. pl. here: deine Gesellen)
glossary.gestanden: stehen — stood (past participle: hatte gestanden, had stood)
glossary.handeln: handeln — to act, to behave (infinitive; treulos handeln, to act faithlessly)
glossary.hielt: halten — held (3rd sg. past; hielt sich daran, held on to it; hielt ein (einhalten), left off)
glossary.hob: heben — lifted, raised (3rd sg. past; hob … hinauf, lifted up; hob in die Höhe, raised up)
glossary.ihm: ihm — to him, for him (dative of er; also to it)
glossary.lassen: lassen — to let, to leave (in Ruhe lassen: to leave in peace); also to have something done
glossary.lauft: laufen — run! (2nd pl. imperative: lauft, run, the two of you)
glossary.ließen: lassen — let, left (3rd pl. past; liegen lassen: to leave lying, to leave behind)
glossary.lust: die Lust — delight, pleasure; desire (ihre größte Lust: her greatest delight)
glossary.nu: der Nu — instant (only in im Nu, in an instant)
glossary.reihe: die Reihe — turn (die Reihe ist an mir: it is my turn); also a row, line
glossary.reitet: reiten — rides (3rd sg. present: der reitet zuerst, he rides first)
glossary.sags: sags — sag es, say it, tell it (imperative sg. of sagen run together with es)
glossary.sank: sinken — sank (3rd sg. past; here zusammensinken, to sink down, collapse)
glossary.schritte: der Schritt — step, stride (acc. pl. here: ein paar Schritte, a few steps)
glossary.see: der See — lake (masc.; die See, fem., would be the sea)
glossary.seidenen: seiden — silken, of silk (adj., dat. pl. here: an den seidenen Kleidern)
glossary.stahl: der Stahl — steel (the metal; von Stahl, of steel)
glossary.stellte: stellen — placed, set (3rd sg. past; hinstellen, to set down; sich stellen als …, to pretend)
glossary.stille: die Stille — stillness, quiet (noun; in nächtlicher Stille, in the stillness of the night)
glossary.treue: die Treue — faith, fidelity, troth (noun; auf Treue die Hand geben, to give one’s hand upon faith)
glossary.volk: das Volk — folk, people, crowd (neuter noun)
glossary.waldhaus: das Waldhaus — forest house, house in the wood (Wald + Haus)
glossary.weckst: wecken — (you) wake, rouse (2nd sg. present: weckst mich aus dem Schlaf)
glossary.weg: der Weg — way, road, path (masc. noun; the same spelling is also weg, away)
glossary.weiß: wissen — (I) know (1st sg. present; the identical spelling weiß also means ‘white’, but here it is the verb)
glossary.wirbel: der Wirbel — drum roll (einen Wirbel schlagen: to beat a roll)
glossary.wärmt: wärmen — warms (3rd sg. present: das wärmt mir die alten Knochen)
glossary.zieh: ziehen — draw off! be off! (imperative sg.; here abziehen: zieh … ab, withdraw)
glossary.zogen: ziehen — moved, drifted (3rd pl. past; here wegziehen, to move off, of clouds)
glossary.zusammenschlugen: zusammenschlagen — closed together over, struck together (3rd pl. past; separable zusammen-)
